hero.label: WorkBuddy Integration
hero.title: Bring RedNote & Douyin data into WorkBuddy: one MCP, one research skill
hero.description: MediaClaw gives WorkBuddy two things: a RedNote (Xiaohongshu) and Douyin MCP server whose 40+ tools collect posts, videos, comments and account data and dedupe them into structured results, and a content research skill whose 12 written methods handle teardowns, topic picks and drafting. Once it is connected you do not decide what to collect or memorise any command — say what you are working on and where you are stuck.
hero.tip: You need the MediaClaw browser extension installed and an active membership first. The agent can only use capabilities you approved in the extension, and every page visit still happens in your own browser.

tasks.title: What one sentence gets you once WorkBuddy is connected
tasks.description: These are real MediaClaw Agent runs and the prompts are copy-ready. Every host runs the same MCP tools and the same methods, so the output is identical; the chat window in these screenshots may not match yours, but what comes back does.

items.title: Turn one post's comment section into a topic list
items.description: A comment section looks full of demand until you try to read it one row at a time. Hand over the link: 322 comments dedupe to 280 distinct texts, 99 of them explicit needs (35.4%), grouped into tool cost / text version of videos / zero-to-one tutorials / can't-ship problems, then delivered as a prioritized topic list and a multi-sheet workbook.

image.alt: A RedNote comment section turned into a prioritized topic list and a multi-sheet workbook

items.title: See one topic across RedNote and Douyin at once
items.description: Scrolling both apps yourself, it is easy to mistake one creator's demo for an official new feature. Hand it over: it first pins down which product the keyword means, reuses the existing RedNote sample, back-fills only Douyin, then groups recent patterns into 7 categories with examples and changelog links.

image.alt: Cross-platform topic research across RedNote and Douyin, grouped into seven patterns with sources

items.title: Chasing a trend — today's posts only
items.description: “Show me RedNote posts about <keyword> published today.” 80 posts from that day scanned as of 23:48, grouped by content direction with the current top performers listed. Put that one line on a daily schedule and it becomes lightweight monitoring.

image.alt: Pulling only the current day's RedNote posts and grouping them by direction

items.title: Findings land in your documents, not in a chat log
items.description: The one thing the extension cannot do alone. “File these comments into <knowledge base path> and put the conclusion at the top.” 1,000 comments land in the document with likes, region and timestamps, opening with core conclusions, theme signals, disagreements and unmet needs — and a reviewable diff before anything is written. Three months later you can still query that library.

image.alt: Comment analysis written into a local knowledge base document, conclusions first

setup.title: Getting connected: three steps, no terminal, no config file
setup.description: WorkBuddy supports fully automatic installation, same as Codex. You do two things: copy a prompt, and approve once.

items.title: Step 1: Copy the install prompt from the extension
items.description: Open System settings → Agent access in the extension, turn on “Allow local agents to call MediaClaw”, expand “Connect Agent”, and hit Copy on the WorkBuddy row. The prompt already carries the official source, WorkBuddy's plugin-manager commands and the repair steps — you do not need to read or edit it.

image.alt: MediaClaw's Agent access panel: enabling local agent calls and copying the WorkBuddy install prompt

items.title: Step 2: Send it to WorkBuddy and let it install itself
items.description: Paste it into a new WorkBuddy conversation as-is. It registers the official marketplace through its own plugin manager, installs the package, detects Windows/macOS/Linux and x64/ARM64, and fetches and verifies the matching runtime. If an older installer left a conflicting mediaclaw MCP entry, it explains and removes it rather than leaving two.

image.alt: Sending the MediaClaw install prompt to WorkBuddy and letting it run the installation

items.title: Step 3: Approve in the extension, it re-checks itself
items.description: A pending device appears in the Agent access tab. Check the name and fingerprint, hit Approve. This run finished in 2m49s with “MediaClaw Agent (WorkBuddy)” authorized; it re-checked the connection on its own and walked through what you can hand it — no need to reply “approved”.

image.alt: WorkBuddy paired successfully: the device is authorized and the first-run welcome is shown

stack.title: What actually gets installed into WorkBuddy
stack.description: One install brings two pieces. They answer “where does the data come from” and “what order do I work in once it arrives” — your own files complete the set.

items.title: MCP server: where the data comes from
items.description: 40+ tools sit in WorkBuddy's tool list over standard STDIO. Which ones it calls, and how often, follows from the task — you never specify them.
features: Content: posts, videos, profile feeds, search results, comments
Enrichment: detail back-fill, image text recognition, video transcripts
Research: keyword scans and long-tail expansion, account scans, benchmark discovery
Reuse: read collections, analyses and style profiles already saved in the extension

items.title: Research skill: what order to work in
items.description: 12 fixed methods, covering everything from “is this niche worth entering” to “is this draft shippable”. It follows them rather than improvising once data lands.
features: Judge first: keyword trends, long-tail demand, benchmark accounts, account strategy, recent hits
Then take apart: a single post's angle, structure, phrasing and engagement signals
Then produce: topics, content briefs, outlines, drafts, adapted to your style
Self-check before delivery: is every claim backed, is a guess written as fact, is it too close to the source

items.title: Your files: why this could only be yours
items.description: A local Markdown folder is enough; Obsidian, Notion or Lark work too. MediaClaw knows what is happening on the platforms — only your library knows who you are.
features: The overlap is the topic list: wanted on the platform ∩ never written by you
When nothing in your files backs a point, it says what is missing instead of padding
Each study lands back in your docs, so next time you query the library instead of re-collecting

items.question: Why must I fully reopen WorkBuddy after installing?
items.answer: A host will not hot-load a new skill or MCP into a running conversation. If the install record changed but the old process is still running, it is not installed yet — and a new conversation inside that same process does not count either. Quit fully and reopen; the agent re-checks the running version, only announces success when it matches the target, and then picks your unfinished request back up.

items.question: Can my model quota handle driving it from WorkBuddy?
items.answer: Far cheaper than letting an agent click through a browser page by page. Collection, pagination and rate-limit cooldowns all run inside the extension and use no host model quota; the extension hands back only structured results. Quota goes to three things: understanding your request, issuing calls and reading results, and the analysis and writing. It also reuses existing data before collecting anything new, and previews large payloads before paging into detail.

items.question: Is this an MCP? Do I configure it by hand in WorkBuddy's plugin manager?
items.answer: It is a standard MCP integration over STDIO, but you never configure it by hand. Send it the install prompt copied from the extension and it registers the official marketplace through WorkBuddy's own plugin manager, installs the package, then detects your OS and chip and fetches and verifies the matching runtime.

items.question: I configured mediaclaw manually before — will it conflict?
items.answer: You will not end up with two. If it finds a user-level mediaclaw MCP entry left by an older installer, it explains and removes the conflict so the official plugin is what runs. Downloading the repo, writing config, or completing one temporary MCP handshake does not count as installed — it goes by what the plugin manager actually lists.

items.question: Do I still need the browser extension running?
items.answer: Yes. The agent package cannot run alone and does not replace the extension. Every page visit goes through the extension in your own browser using sessions you are already signed into, and the agent can only touch capabilities you approved there.

items.question: How do I stay in control of scope and credits?
items.answer: Approving the pairing only allows the connection. Before any new collection it states the source, time range, volume, what it will read and the cost boundary, and waits. Billable capabilities such as transcripts quote estimated credits and your balance separately. “Sure”, “ok”, “go ahead” all confirm — no fixed phrase — and several searches can be approved once and run back to back. Silence is not consent, and anything beyond the approved scope is asked again.

items.question: Are my sessions and data safe?
items.answer: Collection runs in your own browser and the session is never handed to the agent. Never paste cookies, tokens, activation codes or device keys into a conversation, issue or log — the agent will not ask. Revoking one agent's authorization leaves your other approved agents alone.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: The browser extension itself is free. Agent access requires an active membership, and billable capabilities such as video transcripts need credits plus a confirmation before they run. Analysis, generation and reporting on the agent side cost no MediaClaw credits.

items.question: How is this different from Codex or Doubao for Work?
items.answer: The capabilities are identical — same package, same MCP tools, same skill. WorkBuddy and Codex can both hand install and upgrades to the agent end to end. Doubao for Work has no automatic install entry yet, so you save a STDIO connector by hand under Skills · Connectors, and it does not auto-update.
